title: Cylinder
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. Begin by drawing a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. In the first loop, draw four lines to form a rectangle: start the first line at the origin (0.0, 0.0) and end it at (0.075, 0.0). Continue with the second line from (0.075, 0.0) to (0.075, 0.0375), the third line from (0.075, 0.0375) to (0.0, 0.0375), and the fourth line from (0.0, 0.0375) back to the origin. Apply a sketch scale of 0.075 to the rectangle. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into three dimensions by rotating it using Euler angles of zero and translating it with a vector of zero. Extrude the two-dimensional sketch along the normal direction by 0.75 units and do not extrude in the opposite direction. Ensure that this extrusion creates a new solid body. The resulting shape is a cylinder with a rectangular cross-section at the top, measuring 0.075 units in length, 0.0375 units in width, and 0.75 units in height.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the sketch for the rectangular section
sketch = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0, 0).lineTo(0.075, 0).lineTo(0.075, 0.0375).lineTo(0, 0.0375).close()

# Extrude the sketch to create the rectangular section
extruded_section = sketch.extrude(0.75)

# The final model 'r' is the extruded section
r = extruded_section

# Display the final model

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a sketch on the XY plane
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.075, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.075, 0.0375) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0375) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create a rectangular prism
r = r.extrude(0.75)
